I found this book among the ruins of Ashenreach.

The pages are damaged.

Some are missing.

Others have been ruined by time, fire, or something I cannot identify.

But the final entries remain.

They were written by the King himself.

I know this because his name appears beneath the first entry.
I will record his words as they were written.

THE KING'S RECORD

We were greedy.

That is the truth I can no longer deny.

We saw the wealth of this land and convinced ourselves that we deserved all of it.

We took.

We conquered.

We looted.

We destroyed.

Every victory made us want another.

And somewhere along the way...

we forgot why we were fighting in the first place.

We were once people.

We lived together.

We shared this land.

Now we fight our own kind for things that will not matter when we are gone.

But I fear we have gone too far.

During our search, we found something.

Something I cannot explain.

There was a light.

It was calm.

It felt peaceful.

And beside it...

there was darkness.

The darkness felt different.

It felt powerful.

Almost as if it was waiting for us.

My people wanted the darkness.

They believed its power would make us unstoppable.

I allowed them to take it.

Perhaps that was my greatest mistake.

Since then, things have changed.

Our soldiers have become stronger.

But something about them is different.

Some say they feel watched.

Others refuse to speak about what they have seen.

One soldier returned from the lower chambers yesterday.

He would not tell us what happened.

He only asked that we seal the doors.

We did not.

The council believes the power belongs to us now.

They have begun moving it deeper into the kingdom.

I told them to stop.

They did not listen.

I have begun to wonder if we truly found power...

or if the power found us.

Tonight I walked through the barracks.

Our soldiers were preparing for tomorrow.

They looked stronger than any army we have ever raised.

Yet none of them spoke.

They simply stood there.

Watching the walls.

I asked one of them what he was looking at.

He said there was someone standing behind me.

I turned.

There was no one there.

When I looked back at him...

he was gone.

I searched the entire barracks.

Nothing.

No footprints.

No blood.

Nothing.

I have ordered the lower chambers sealed.

The council has refused.

They say we need the power.

They say tomorrow's battle will decide the future of Ashenreach.

Perhaps they are right.

Perhaps I am simply afraid.
But I cannot shake the feeling that we are no longer alone.

Tomorrow, we march.

It will be the greatest battle this kingdom has ever seen.

I can feel it.

Something is going to happen.

I do not know what.

But something is coming.

Perhaps this war will finally end everything.

Perhaps it will save us.

I no longer know.

All I know is that we were too greedy.

Too blind.

We wanted everything.

And now...

I fear we may lose everything.

If anyone finds these pages after tomorrow...

remember this.
Every action has a consequence.
And ours has finally come.

MY NOTES

That was the last entry.

There were no more pages after it.

The arena outside the ruins looks as though it may have once been part of the battlefield described in the book.

But I cannot prove it.

I searched the ruins for the lower chambers mentioned by the King.

I found them.

The doors were still sealed.

At least...

I believe they were.

There are marks around the entrance.

Something had tried to open them from the inside.

I found no body.

No weapon.

Nothing that tells me what happened.

But there was one thing.

A symbol.

The same symbol I found beneath the older ruins.

I thought it belonged to the people who lived here before the kingdoms.

I am no longer certain.

Whatever Ashenreach found...

it was not theirs.

And somehow, the power they found still remains.

I do not know what it is.

But after reading this...

I am not sure I want to find out.
